items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: my aunt my mother‟s youngest sister was a few years older then I and she was always in charge of me.

ctx.x: Well what happened, before I left, the day I left… I was eight years old. One of my uncles… somebody in the family had gotten sick and my aunt my mother‟s youngest sister was a few years older then I and she was always in charge of me. We had gone to the hospital and on our way back from the hospital we had to go right down Clay Street. There was a big crowd in the middle of the street. It was like seven or eight o‟clock at night and I looked at this crowd, we had to go right by there, and they had a black man…

For most people who lived there… it‟s difficult for anyone who didn‟t live through that to understand the difference between the extended family that you described, both in Chicago and in Mississippi, where you really did look out for your neighbor‟s children and your friends, and everybody was…
